title: Hollywood's AI Split Shows Who Figures It Out First
metaDescription: Scorsese gets AI while others resist. The people already building AI skills are pulling ahead. Here's what actually matters.
author: Marty @ CertFlo

sections.heading: Some People Get It, Some Don't
sections.body: Everyone thinks Hollywood's AI thing is about art versus tech. Nah. It's just about who adapts and who sits there complaining. Director Boots Riley went off on Martin Scorsese for embracing AI, saying the guy "doesn't give a f*ck" about AI's impact but took "a gang of money" for some advisor position. Deadline says Riley's mad about Scorsese's "attempt to push the industry toward" generative AI. But Riley's missing the point. Scorsese isn't selling out. Dude's just not gonna be left behind. That's what smart people do when something this big shows up.

sections.heading: This Is Happening Everywhere
sections.body:
Hollywood's split is playing out in every job right now. You got the people fighting it cause they think they're protecting something. Then you got the people who see AI automation as the biggest edge they're gonna get.

Guess who's already winning?

The marketing person who figured out AI copywriting is cranking out campaigns 3x faster than everyone else. The accountant using AI for data stuff is finding things that make executives pay attention. The project manager who automated the boring stuff has time to think about the big picture.

They're not replacing creativity. They're just getting better at it.

sections.heading: The Gap Is Already Opening
sections.body: Here's what the people complaining don't get: AI skills aren't some future thing anymore. This is happening right now. While everyone else argues about ethics and whatever, the smart ones are quietly building stuff that separates them. Learning prompt engineering. Automating the repetitive tasks. Using AI to research faster, write better, think deeper. Every day they wait is another day someone else gets further ahead. The early adopter window is closing fast. Soon AI literacy won't be an advantage — it'll just be expected. The people building these skills now are setting themselves up for promotions and opportunities that won't even exist for the holdouts. For those serious about proving their value to leadership through strategic AI implementation, having a structured approach to documenting efficiency gains becomes crucial.

sections.heading: Your Call
sections.body:
Scorsese gets it. At 82 he could just coast on being a legend. Instead he's learning new tools that'll make his next films better.

That's the difference between winners and everyone else.
